### Architect · Answer

Event: `8cef452f7b6ccc9dfe7e06d087e6bcf4` · 2026-10-05T01:06:21Z

> The direct unshare probe is too strong as a prerequisite: failure does NOT establish rootless Podman failure. `unshare -Ur` attempts the caller-to-root single-ID mapping directly, not the subordinate-ID helper path. The recorded uid_map error shows that write failed, not why; it does not test newuidmap/newgidmap. Mode4755 proves installation, not successful setuid execution or mapping.
> 
> Podman5.4.2's becomeRootInUserNS/tryMappingTool uses newuidmap/newgidmap for configured subids, mapping 0 to the invoking UID/GID plus the subordinate range; a configured-range helper error is fatal. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v5.4.2/pkg/rootless/rootless_linux.go . Comparison: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/util-linux/util-linux/v2.41/sys-utils/unshare.c (not verification of installed util-linux build).
> 
> Smallest meaningful proposed probe, INSIDE the identical reviewed image/container as dev with recorded HOME/runtime-dir/vfs settings and primary group:
> `sg dev -c 'podman --log-level=debug --cgroup-manager=cgroupfs unshare cat /proc/self/uid_map /proc/self/gid_map'`
> Documented mapping diagnostic: https://docs.podman.io/en/v5.4.2/markdown/podman-unshare.1.html . Expect each map to contain `0 1447391350 1` and `1 3713496320 65536`; preserve full output and exit status. No rootless-netns flag, image pull/build, container workload or test.
> 
> This changes the probe, not isolation/permissions. But it is new execution after the approved stop-on-failure: existing approval does not authorize restarting/repeating. Seek bounded continuation before running; stopped container stays stopped now. Podman may initialize local state/namespaces, so execution is not read-only. Success proves the mapping path only, not cgroup operation, image build, SSH or the gate; failure identifies its stage, not an AppArmor cause. No run or file edit performed.
